opportunities.title: Fix and rebuild the front door: an agent-readable site plus a scoped project-inquiry intake
opportunities.problem: Menlo's public front door does not work. The home page renders with no h1, roughly 431 characters of visible text, one paragraph, no address and no call to action, and the phone number is plain text with no tel: link. The Projects index and News index print the page-builder shortcode as literal text, so the 3,000-project portfolio and the June 2026 Greek Real Estate Partners announcement are unreachable from the menu, and the Project Map page holds only an empty iframe. Structured data is Organization-only with a telephone and no address or ProfessionalService type, so an AI assistant asked for a civil engineer in Middlesex County has almost nothing on the page to ground an answer in. New inquiries land in a four-field form (Name, Email, Phone, Message) with no municipality, block/lot, project type, timeline or file upload, and it is protected by reCAPTCHA v3 plus a honeypot, so an automated intake path is blocked before it starts. All of this sits behind a listing that shows only three reviews, the newest about eight years old.
evidence: Rendered home page has no h1 element, about 431 characters of visible text in one paragraph, one image, and JSON-LD limited to BreadcrumbList, Organization, WebPage and WebSite with a telephone but no address and no LocalBusiness/ProfessionalService type — https://menloeng.com/

Projects index and News index render the Divi page-builder shortcode as literal text, so no projects or news items are displayed; the Project Map page contains only an empty iframe container — https://menloeng.com/projects/

A real June 26, 2026 project post exists (281,215-SF Class A industrial facility, 169 Lackawanna Avenue, Parsippany) but the News index that should list it is broken — https://menloeng.com/congratulations-to-greek-real-estate-partners-on-169-lackawanna-avenue/
Contact form is Gravity Forms 3.2.2 with reCAPTCHA v3 and a honeypot, and collects only Name, Email, Phone and Message: no scope, parcel, timeline or upload fields — https://menloeng.com/contact-us/

Google Maps shows a 5.0 rating for 'Menlo Engineering Associates Inc' but the review count is not visible in the limited view; a third-party listing shows 5.0 from 3 reviews, newest about eight years old — https://reviews.birdeye.com/menlo-engineering-associates-inc-144684430385065
robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/ and publishes a sitemap, so crawlers and AI agents are not restricted from reading the site — https://menloeng.com/robots.txt

Prior browser review scored agent readiness findable 3/5, answerable 2/5, bookable 2/5 and recorded no CTA and no quote or booking engine (triage.json, sources https://menloeng.com/ and https://menloeng.com/contact-us/)
opportunities.agent_design: Two layers. (1) Static rebuild: a new home page with an h1, a services/project-type/sector summary drawn from the six published service lines and the named client roster, the Highland Park address, a tel: link and one 'Start a project' CTA; repair the Projects and News index templates so posts and project entries actually render; populate the project map or remove it; upgrade JSON-LD to ProfessionalService with address, geo, areaServed (NJ counties served), hasOfferCatalog of the six services and openingHours, matching the contact page; refresh the stale 2024 footer. (2) Agent layer: a form-to-queue intake agent that captures municipality, block/lot, project type, rough acreage/SF, timeline and a plan or survey upload, classifies the inquiry against the six service lines and the client roster, dedupes repeat/known clients, and opens a structured record. A follow-up agent acknowledges inquiries inside and outside 8:30-5, chases anything unanswered after one business day, and assembles a one-page qualification brief for the responsible project manager. Human approval: every outbound reply and every qualification brief is approved by a project manager before it leaves; no pricing is quoted by the agent. Keep reCAPTCHA on the public form but add a plain, machine-readable services/hours/contact block and a direct mailto so an assistant can still route an inquiry.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: No chatbot subscription repairs Divi shortcode breakage, corrects schema, or connects an intake form to a routed queue and a follow-up cadence. The work needs WordPress template-level editing, structured-data work, a document-upload path, and an agent that holds state across inquiries — plus reCAPTCHA handling that a customer-facing bot cannot do on its own.

impact_estimate.range: No revenue claim. Customer-visible today: 0 project entries and 0 news items rendered on the two index pages, ~431 characters of indexable home-page copy, no home-page CTA. Recoverable staff time (inference): roughly 1-2 hours/week of engineer or PM time spent reading and re-keying unstructured inquiries, about $2.6k-$5.2k/yr at the NJ civil engineer average hourly wage of $50.32; missed after-hours inquiries are not measurable from public data.
impact_estimate.assumptions: 3-6 inquiries/week (inferred from a 3,000-project history, a six-person key-personnel roster and no published lead volume); 15-20 minutes of manual triage per inquiry today because the form has no scope fields; 46 working weeks/year; wage is the BLS/OEWS NJ average for civil engineers, used as the cost of the person doing the triage, not as a revenue estimate. The 2026 ACEC report's finding that most engineering firms already use AI in marketing and sales is context, not a measured saving at this firm.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: repaired Projects/News/Project Map templates, a new home page with h1, services, sectors, address, tel: link and one CTA, ProfessionalService schema with address, areaServed and services, a scoped project-inquiry form with file upload and a routing/qualification agent, and a four-week before/after count of inquiries, response time and rendered project/news entries.

opportunities.title: Bid and board-hearing radar that also drafts the proposal
opportunities.problem: Menlo wins work through relationships, referrals and municipal-board appearances, with no system for spotting new opportunities. A developer's application surfaces when a town posts an agenda, and there is no tooling anywhere on the site or in the visible footprint — no CRM, no chat, no pipeline — so the radar is whatever a principal happens to read. The firm is simultaneously hiring a Project Manager P.E. at $120K-$135K whose stated job is managing site and subdivision plans through land-development approvals, and six named key personnel are already project managers, which puts a lot of senior hours into chasing approvals, assembling proposal and qualification material, and preparing for evening hearings.
evidence: Open Project Manager P.E. role, $120K-$135K, requires 5+ years managing site and subdivision plans through land-development approvals; a parallel designer role at $75k-$90k requires NJDEP stormwater rules — https://menloeng.com/our-company/careers/

Riverdale Planning Board minutes of November 13, 2025 record 'Scott Turner of Menlo Engineering Associates' sworn in as the first expert for application 2025-11, i.e. recurring in-person municipal board testimony — https://www.riverdalenj.gov/_Content/pdf/minutes/2025-11-13-PB-Minutes.pdf

Firm claims over 3,000 planning and design projects since 1966 for developers, retailers, institutions and municipalities, implying many concurrent sites across many jurisdictions — https://menloeng.com/our-company/

No CRM, chat widget, booking tool or client portal is present on any page checked; forms are Gravity Forms only, with Google Analytics 4 (G-02HM33KMW5) measuring traffic that no lead pipeline follows — https://menloeng.com/contact-us/

ACEC Research Institute 2025 report (association survey of 644 firm leaders plus 19 interviews): AI use is most common in marketing and sales at 81% versus 36% in design and project delivery, and AI-assisted proposal development is named a common application — https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/

O*NET Civil Engineers (17-2051.00) lists 'prepare or present public reports on topics such as bid proposals, deeds, environmental impact statements, or right-of-way descriptions' as a core task (importance 63), alongside estimating quantities and cost of materials, equipment or labor (64) — https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/17-2051.00

NJ Department of State maintains a statewide legal-notices directory linking public entities' notice pages, and municipalities publish planning/zoning agendas separately, so discovery means many heterogeneous sources — https://www.nj.gov/state/statewide-legal-notices-list.shtml
opportunities.agent_design: A discovery agent watches a defined source list — the NJ statewide legal-notices directory, the planning/zoning board agenda and minutes pages of a named set of target municipalities, and county and municipal bid pages — on a daily crawl, parses agenda and notice PDFs, and extracts applicant, site address, block/lot, application type (site plan, subdivision, variance, redevelopment) and hearing date. It matches each application against the firm's client roster, market sectors and geography, then produces a weekly go/no-go brief with a short reason and a suggested point of contact where the applicant is not already a client. A second agent assembles the response side: pulls the relevant past proposal and fee history for that work type from the firm's own library, drafts the technical-approach and scope sections, generates the submission checklist for that municipality, and once a hearing is scheduled, maintains a hearing calendar with exhibit and filing deadlines, board-packet requirements and travel reminders, and drafts the confirmation and follow-up correspondence to the client. Systems touched: municipal websites and PDFs, the firm's document library, calendars, email. Human approval: a principal approves every go/no-go call, every proposal before it is sent, and every calendar commitment; the agent never submits an application, bid or proposal.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is hundreds of heterogeneous municipal sources with no shared format, plus PDF agenda parsing, entity matching against a client list, retrieval from the firm's own past proposals and two-way calendar integration. An off-the-shelf assistant cannot crawl and remember 50-100 town sites, and a generic chatbot cannot know which of Menlo's prior proposals is the right precedent or which board's packet rules apply.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly 2-5 hours/week of project-manager and principal time recovered from opportunity screening, proposal assembly and hearing logistics — about $5.2k-$13.1k/yr at the NJ civil engineer average of $50.32/hour, before any value from earlier notice of a new application. Treat the top of the range as unproven at a firm this size.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Scoping from a mid-size-firm transfer of two measured results, both discounted: the peer-reviewed experiment with 453 professionals found a 40% cut in completion time on professional writing tasks with ChatGPT, and the peer-reviewed BCG field experiment found 25.1% faster work on tasks inside the AI frontier — consultants and professionals, not civil engineers. Applied to 6-12 senior hours/week of proposal and approval-chasing work, that implies 2.5-4.8 hours saved; rounded conservatively to 2-5. 46 working weeks/year. Any revenue from newly spotted applications is deliberately excluded because no public data shows the firm's win rate or proposal volume.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: source list of 10-15 target municipalities plus the NJ legal-notices directory live, one weekly go/no-go brief delivered, two proposal drafts built from the firm's own past proposals for a real pending opportunity, and a hearing calendar with deadlines for the next two scheduled board appearances. Success measured as hours of PM time per brief versus the firm's current manual routine.

opportunities.title: Private plan-review and stormwater compliance knowledge agent (the institutional memory problem)
opportunities.problem: Every land-development submission comes back with a municipal or board engineer's review letter, and each comment has to be answered point by point against NJDEP stormwater rules (N.J.A.C. 7:8) and the local ordinance, usually by the same senior people who are now leaving. The firm's own announcement has two principals moving to part-time advisory roles ahead of retirement, while the new designer posting demands working knowledge of NJDEP stormwater rules and the PM posting demands the approvals process. That judgement currently lives in individuals' heads and in decades of past comment letters sitting in project folders, and nothing on the public profile shows a document system that would let a new hire retrieve it.
evidence: Careers posting requires NJDEP stormwater rules knowledge and grading/drainage design in AutoCAD Civil 3D for the $75k-$90k role, and land-development approvals experience for the $120K-$135K PM role — https://menloeng.com/our-company/careers/

Firm announcement names the new officer team and says Fred Coco and Jule Szalay moved to part-time advisory roles ahead of retirement — https://menloeng.com/menlo-engineering-proudly-announces-our-new-executive-team/

Six published service lines including Wetland & Environmental, Highway Design and Construction Administration, i.e. overlapping regulatory regimes on the same projects — https://menloeng.com/services/

NJDEP maintains the stormwater management rule N.J.A.C. 7:8 with a current amendment and publishes which version applies to a project, so rule text is versioned and must be cited accurately — https://dep.nj.gov/stormwater/stormwater-management/stormwater-management-rule-n-j-a-c-78/

ACEC Research Institute 2025 report names code-compliance checking and proposal drafting among tasks that now take minutes rather than hours, while only 36% of firms use AI in design and project delivery — https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/

Industry constraint: AI cannot replace the judgement of a licensed Professional Engineer and output must be reviewed and sealed by the responsible licensee, so every draft needs a PE gate (industry.json constraints, NCEES/state board guidance scope)

Client confidentiality and NDA exposure dominate consultancies, and Menlo's clients include national retailers and homebuilders plus municipalities, which argues for private rather than public model deployment (industry.json constraints)
opportunities.agent_design: A private, retrieval-only knowledge agent indexed over the firm's own material: past municipal review letters and the responses that resolved them, approved plan checklists by municipality, the current NJDEP N.J.A.C. 7:8 text and BMP manual, and submission requirements for the towns the firm works in — running in a client-scoped, access-controlled environment so one developer's file is never retrievable from another's query. Triggers: (a) a new review letter is uploaded, and the agent extracts each comment, classifies it (stormwater quantity/quality, recharge, sight distance, utilities, landscape, wetland buffer), drafts a point-by-point response with the cited rule or ordinance section and the closest prior firm response as precedent, and flags anything that needs engineering judgement rather than precedent; (b) a pre-submittal run, where a plan set and checklist are compared and a gap list is produced before the package goes to the board. A weekly digest reports which municipal reviewers raise which repeated comments, so the firm can fix issues upstream. Human approval: every draft is reviewed, corrected and sealed by the responsible P.E.; nothing is submitted automatically and the agent never asserts code compliance as a conclusion, only cites and drafts.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot index thousands of the firm's own PDFs and CAD-adjacent documents with per-client access control, cannot keep a versioned regulatory corpus (the stormwater rule was amended and the applicable version depends on the project), and cannot produce an auditable citation trail a P.E. can defend at a hearing. Putting client plan data into a public model would breach the confidentiality terms the industry's constraints call out.

impact_estimate.range: About 2-8 engineering hours per review-letter cycle likely reducible to 1-3, i.e. roughly $2.4k-$7.2k/yr of engineer time across 2-4 cycles a month, with the larger and unquantified value being a shorter approval timeline and less dependence on the two retiring principals.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Review-letter response cycle today 4-8 engineer hours; 2-4 cycles/month; a conservative 25-40% draftable share, discounted from the 40% time reduction measured on professional writing tasks in the peer-reviewed Science experiment (453 professionals, simulated 20-30 minute writing tasks, not plan review). 46 working weeks/year, $50.32/hour NJ civil engineer average. Scaling up is deliberately excluded because headcount, project volume and current documentation practices are not publicly verifiable.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks on one live project: index 40-60 past review letters and responses, the current N.J.A.C. 7:8 rule text and two municipal submission checklists; produce a full draft response to one real municipal review letter and a pre-submittal gap list for one plan set, with the PM scoring each drafted comment as usable / needs edit / unusable. Deliverable includes the accuracy log, because that log is what decides whether this expands.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (21/30): the front-door failure is fully verified — no h1, ~431 characters of home-page text, Projects and News indexes rendering raw shortcodes, an empty Project Map iframe and Organization-only schema without an address — and the hiring of a $75k-$90k designer plus a $120K-$135K P.E. project manager is verified backlog pressure. Deductions because the operational pain is inferred: there is no CRM or portal evidence, no complaints or negative reviews, and only three old reviews, so day-to-day friction is reasoned from absence rather than observed. Fit (17/20): G, B and C are core consultancy capabilities and the firm's work (municipal filings, board testimony, proposals, stormwater compliance) maps almost one-to-one onto discovery, document-drafting and knowledge agents; the deduction is that no engineering-design work is addressable by an agent, and PE sealing limits autonomy. Ability to pay (14/20): a 60-year-old civil engineering firm billing per-project site work on 281,215-SF industrial facilities, with two open roles priced $75k-$135k, so budget exists; but revenue, headcount and margins are unverified (LinkedIn and Indeed blocked; third-party estimates range 11-50 vs 1-24), and the leadership transition adds spending uncertainty. Ease (11/15): small decision group (President Gregory Oman, then Scott Turner as the named operational contact), WordPress/Divi site the firm already pays a designer to maintain, no legacy CRM to displace; deductions for the reCAPTCHA-blocked form, for six-plus named PMs who all need to accept a new intake flow, and for a firm with no published after-hours culture. Strategic (13/15): the same three problems — broken Divi-era front door, municipal-agenda blindness, review-letter treadmill — exist at essentially every small NJ land-development consultancy, so the front-door rebuild and the bid radar are packaged and resold with a new source list and new municipal rulebook. Physical/edge (E) was deliberately not proposed: avenues.json is not in this folder, and the profile shows no physical operations footprint — one office, weekday hours, deliverables are documents and drawings, no fleet, shop floor, dock, kitchen or inventory — so camera/sensor work has nothing to attach to. If a walk-in shows a survey/field crew or a yard, that judgement should be revisited.

best_evidence_signal: The rendered home page has no h1 and about 431 characters of visible text, and the Projects index prints page-builder shortcode instead of any project — the firm's 60 years of work is invisible to both visitors and AI assistants (https://menloeng.com/projects/)
suggested_channel: walk-in at 261 Cleveland Avenue, Highland Park with a printed one-page front-door audit (home page screenshot, the broken Projects page, and the schema gap), then email to Gregory S. Oman, President
